spans.text: Our Father, our King, (even if we are not deserving) act with mercy toward us for the glory of Your great and awesome Name that the world intuitively knows rests on us, Your people.
Our Father, our King, be kind to us and answer us, even though we do not have good deeds; treat us with leniency and loving-kindness and save us.

וְהוּא רַחוּם יְכַפֵּר עָוֹן—We admit that it is because of our own sins that we, Your nation, and Your holy city Yerushalayim have become an object of scorn among the nations (which is a huge chillul Hashem). We ask that You save us and Your city in the merit of our ancestors and because Your kindness is eternal.

See our desolation and the desolation of Your city Yerushalayim. Though all of that is our own fault, still, if Your nation would perish and if Your city would fall, then the nations of the world would say, "Where is their God?"—which would be a huge chillul Hashem! Therefore, please save us and rebuild Yerushalayim so that everyone will recognize You and Your providence.
Save us and have compassion on us in the merit of the promise (ברית) You made to the Avos that we would be Your eternal nation.
Do not forsake us and do not be far away from us; see all that we have suffered throughout our history. Save us in the merit of the Bris Bein Habesarim and in the merit of Akeidas Yitzchak.

אֵל רַחוּם וְחַנּוּן—Please forgive our sins and save us from all our troubles and sorrows, for You are full of mercy and compassion. The world knows we are Your nation, and the nations recognize Your power by what happens to us!

אֵין כָּמוֹךָ חַנּוּן וְרַחוּם—We will examine our actions, try to improve, and return to You—for You, Hashem, are always open to accepting our teshuvah. Help us achieve our teshuvah and save us from our troubles, for it is only You, Hashem, that we turn to for help.

הַפּוֹתֵחַ יָד בִּתְשׁוּבָה—Though we have not lived up to our potential, please remember the bris with the Avos and our daily proclamations of the Shema, which is our acceptance of You as our only God. Have mercy on Your land and on Your children, and show Your power over Your enemies. And show favor to us, the nation who, with constant love, proclaim twice a day: !שְׁמַע יִשְׂרָאֵל יְהוָה אֱלֹהֵינוּ יְהוָה אֶחָד

וַיֹּאמֶר דָּוִד אֶל גָּד—As David HaMelech said to the prophet Gad: I accept the fact that I have sinned and must be punished, but please, let my punishment come directly from Hashem Himself, since He is merciful, rather than through the hands of humans.
—רַחוּם וְחַנּוּן חָטָאתִי לְפָנֶיךָ I know I have sinned, but I ask, please, Hashem, do not punish me

(—יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, שׁוּב מֵחֲרוֹן אַפֶּךָ As Moshe said to Hashem after the sin of the golden calf, when asking Him to forgive Bnei Yisrael) Hashem, turn back from Your fierce anger; וְהִנָּחֵם עַל הָרָעָה לְעַמֶּךָ—and soften the harsh punishment You intended to inflict on Your people.

We now describe our nation's state of suffering—each followed by the above plea (יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, שׁוּב מֵחֲרוֹן אַפֶּךָ וְהִנָּחֵם עַל הָרָעָה לְעַמֶּךָ) that Hashem should soften His punishment of us.

—הַבֶּט מִשָּׁמַיִם וּרְאֵה We are despised by the nations of the world and are viewed as sheep to be led to the slaughter, to be killed and humiliated. And yet, despite this, we have not forgotten You and Your laws; please do not forget us! יְהֹוָה ...אֱלֹהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
זָרִים—The world says Bnei Yisrael have no future! But we place our hope with You—that Your compassion will suppress Your anger against us....יְהוָה אֱלֹהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
חוּסָה—The hostile masses treat us with cruelty, and they gloat, saying, "Where is their God?" For the glory of Your name, deal kindly with us....יְהוָה אֱלֹהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל

קוֹלֵנוּ תִּשְׁמַע וְתָחוֹן—Do not leave us in the hands of our enemies who want to wipe us out! Remember Your promise to the Avos that we would be as numerous as the stars, yet now we are only a small group among the nations of the world. And yet despite this, we have not forgotten You and Your laws; please do not forget us! ...יְהוָה אֱלֹהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
עָזְרֵנוּ אֱלֹהֵי יִשְׁעֵנוּ—Save us and pardon our sins, for it is through our miraculous survival in history that the world recognizes Your power! יְהוָה אֱלֹהֵי ...יִשְׂרָאֵל
שׁוֹמֵר יִשְׂרָאֵל—You are the guardian of Yisrael; do not let Yisrael perish—in the merit that we say daily שְׁמַע יִשְׂרָאֵל!
שׁוֹמֵר גּוֹי אֶחָד—You are the guardian of the one and only (אֶחָד) unique nation; do not let that one and only (אֶחָד) unique nation perish—in the merit that we say daily that Hashem is אֶחָד!

שׁוֹמֵר גּוֹי קָדוֹשׁ—You are the guardian of the separate and elevated (קָדוֹשׁ) nation; do not let that separate and elevated (קָדוֹשׁ) nation perish—in the merit that we (like the angels) declare daily קָדוֹשׁ קָדוֹשׁ קָדוֹשׁ!
מִתְרַצֶּה בְּרַחֲמִים—There is no power that can save us but You. Though we may not be worthy, deal with us with Your loving-kindness and chessed.

(To sum it all up:) וַאֲנַחְנוּ לֹא נֵדַע—Hashem, we do not know what else we can do, so we turn to You for Your kindness and help. We know we lack merit, but You know that we are material beings and thus have many struggles! Pardon us and give us another chance to prove ourselves, so that we may spread the knowledge of Your Presence to the whole world.

blocks.en: I Am Not Worthy, and We Are Not Worthy, but We Are Asking for Divine Favor—Personally and Nationally

spans.text: והוא רחום / ויאמר דוד / שומר ישראל / ואנחנו לא נדע
For a list of when Tachanun is omitted, see Appendix 12:9.
On all other weekdays, begin with "Short Tachanun" on page 87.

NOTE: The general custom is that women do not say Tachanun (neither the "long Tachanun" nor the "short Tachanun"). Why? The most common explanation is that Tachanun, similar to Maariv, was originally an optional tefillah that women did not accept upon themselves.
FAQ: But why? Why the differences in tefillah (and practices) between men and women?
ANSWER: Very common and complicated question! See Appendix 11.
